target_customer: Event organizers and venues in Mexico and Latin America who sell tickets, and fans buying them
problem: Ticket fraud and scalping hurt fans and organizers, and organizers lack control over primary and resale markets.
business_model: Ticketing fees on primary sales plus controlled resale marketplace

founders.name: Walter Gonzalez
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Founder/CEO; no further background.

founders.name: Roberto Rey
founders.background_notes: YC profile calls him a technical founder trying to fix problems in LATAM.

founders.name: Roberto Novelo
founders.background_notes: YC blog post on Livement names Walter Gonzalez, Roberto Novelo and Roberto Rey as the three co-founders (https://www.ycombinator.com/blog/livement). Not listed on the YC company page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile ticketing with anti-fraud controls, payments and venue entry validation is standard but needs reliability at event scale.

defensibility.rationale: Organizer contracts and venue integrations create some stickiness, but ticketing software is widely replicated.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Ticketmaster and Superboletos still lead large venues in Mexico per a 2025 IQ Magazine report; no source shows them copying or buying Livement.

market_need_then: Ticket scalping and fraud were a known problem in Mexico; a May 2016 Chilango article headline reports a new alternative to Ticketmaster launched in Mexico City (company not identified in the snippet).

branding.domain_note: Company site is boletomovil.com; Livement is the international brand name per YC.

rebrands.why: Not stated; YC lists Livement as the name with Boletomovil used in Latin America.

brand_strength.rationale: Two names are in use (Boletomovil in Latin America, Livement elsewhere) and no brand press, community or merch was found.

outcome_analysis: Livement, sold in Latin America as Boletomovil, is a Guadalajara ticketing company that YC lists as active with 45 people. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news was found and funding is not public beyond aggregator entries, so the outcome is unclear. The market has strong incumbents but also a real fraud and scalping problem.
notes: Aggregators (CB Insights, The Company Check) list one seed of about $120K on 2016-08-24 and name Y Combinator, Redwood and Top Tier Capital Partners; one source dates a seed to November 2023. Unverified single-type aggregator data, so no round is recorded. The company site returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Competitor list empty: only 2025 and 2026 market lists were found; the 2016 Chilango piece did not name the company in the snippet. Name origin not found. Completeness pass: the seed of about $120K dated 2016-08-24 is recorded from CB Insights and rests on a single database (Caplight shows the same $120K total; one source dates a seed to November 2023, unresolved). Roberto Novelo added as co-founder per the YC blog.
